51564172.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to PD-L1 (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface Plasmon: 4.18. Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) Assay. In the progress, the SPR measuring instrument (Nicoya) was prepared according to the initialization setting, and the new carboxyl chip which was purchased from G-BIO company was installed in the corresponding position. The configured receptor protein (PD-L1) was fixed on the chip surface using an amino coupling reagent kit. Subsequently, these target compounds with different concentration gradients were added to evaluate their binding ability with target enzyme (PD-L1), and glycine/HCl with pH 3.0 was used to dissociate the binding system. Finally, these obtained results were analyzed using Trace Drawer software.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Figure 5. Affinity between preferred compounds (L11, L20, L21) and positive control (BPE) with PD-L1 was determined by SPR assay. (A) The KD value of positive control (BPE) with PD-L1 was calculated. (B) The KD value of compound (L11) with PD-L1 was calculated. (C) The KD value of compound (L20) with PD-L1 was calculated. (D) The KD value of compound (L21) with PD-L1 was calculated.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 sensorgram concentration labels: BPE 1.67 mM, BPE 0.56 mM, BPE 0.18 mM, BPE 0.06 mM, BPE 0.02 mM, BPE 0.00 mM
original_paragraph.Results text - SPR analysis: detected using surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and BPE was set as a positive control. The corresponding KD values were calculated and are displayed in Figure 5. These preferred compounds and positive control BPE with different concentration gradient could effectively induce plasmon resonance phenomenon, indicating that these molecular structures possessed a similar binding pathway with PD-L1. It was clearly observed that KD values (3.45e-8–6.55e-8) of preferred compounds (L11, L20, L21) displayed similar affinity levels with BPE (KD: 5.37e-8), which suggested these compounds exerted similar affinity ability with PD-L1. In particular, compound (L20) with the lowest KD value (6.55e-8) exhibited an excellent binding effect with PD-L1.
